translation:
Target defines the proposition (without asserting or proving it) that there exists a system N of type S1 Bool Bool—consisting of a finite type of nodes N.A1, a state type N.A3 n for each node n, an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to each node n, a synchronous update function N.a5 giving the next state of each node n from the current global state and a Boolean input, and a Boolean output function N.a6 of the global state—such that all four of the following hold:
1. (N.D12) In the directed dependency graph on N.A1 where there is an edge from m to n (N.D8 m n) whenever there exist two global states agreeing at every node other than m and a Boolean input on which node n's update N.a5 produces different next states, no two distinct nodes m ≠ n are mutually reachable via non-empty directed paths (i.e., it never holds that there is both a directed path of length ≥ 1 from m to n and a directed path of length ≥ 1 from n to m). Self-loops (a node depending on itself) are allowed, while directed cycles involving two or more distinct nodes are forbidden.
2. (N.D25 2) For every node n in N.A1, its state type N.A3 n is finite and has cardinality at most 2 (since N.a4 n provides an element, it has 1 or 2 states, though the condition only writes finite and ≤ 2).
3. (N.d13 = 3) The node type N.A1 has cardinality exactly 3.
4. (S1.D6 N (d26 8)) For every finite list xs of Booleans (of any length, including the empty list), running N on xs—starting from the initial global state N.a4, updating all nodes simultaneously left-to-right for each input in xs, and applying N.a6 to the resulting global state—produces the same Boolean output as running d26 8 on xs. Here d26 8 is the single-node system with state type Fin 8 (integers 0 through 7 with addition wrapping modulo 8), initial state 0, update rule that adds 1 modulo 8 on input true and leaves the state unchanged on input false, and output true if the final state is 0 and false otherwise (so its output on xs is true if and only if the number of true entries in xs is divisible by 8).

divergences.description: The formal statement specifies Boolean inputs (`S1 Bool Bool`) where `d26 8` increments the counter modulo 8 on `true` and leaves the state unchanged on `false`, whereas the description refers generically to 'the counter modulo 8 after every finite input sequence' without stating this Boolean increment/hold input convention.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement accurately formalizes the existence of a three-unit, at-most-binary, synchronous network with no multi-unit feedback loops that matches the mod-8 zero-count output of `d26 8` on all finite Boolean input sequences, and the author's description accurately represents the passages and the scope of the claim. The only minor omission is that the description does not specify the Lean model's Boolean increment/hold input convention.
